_comment: Kid-level English for each verse, keyed "<chapter>:<verse>". Written by hand at P2/P3 reading level: what the verse is saying, not a formal translation. Read by scripts/build_bible_text.py.
1:1: The wise sayings of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel.
1:2: They help you learn to be wise, and to understand what people mean.
1:3: They teach you to live well: to be kind, to be fair, and to be honest.
1:4: They make a simple person clever, and give a young person knowledge and good sense.
1:5: A wise person listens and learns even more; a clever person learns how to decide well.
1:6: They help you understand wise sayings, word pictures, and riddles.
1:7: Respecting the LORD is where knowledge begins. Only fools look down on wisdom and teaching.
1:8: My son, listen to your father's teaching, and do not turn away from your mother's rules.
1:9: They will be like a beautiful crown on your head and a chain around your neck.
1:10: My son, if bad people try to tempt you, do not go along with them.
1:11: They may say: Come with us! Let's hide and wait, and hurt someone who has done nothing wrong.
1:12: They say: We will swallow them up alive, like a deep pit swallowing people whole.
1:13: They say: We will get all kinds of treasure and fill our houses with what we take.
1:14: They say: Join us! We will all share one money bag together.
1:15: My son, do not walk down that road with them. Keep your feet away from their path.
1:16: Their feet run to do wrong, and they hurry to hurt other people.
1:17: It is no use setting a net where the bird can see it.
1:18: But these people are really hiding to hurt themselves; they are trapping their own lives.
1:19: That is what happens to everyone who is greedy for money: greed takes away their own life.
1:20: Wisdom calls out loudly in the street, and raises her voice in the open square.
1:21: She shouts at the busy corner, at the city gate, and all through the town.
1:22: She says: You simple people, how long will you love being foolish? How long will you laugh at what is good and hate knowing things?
1:23: Turn around and listen when I correct you! Then I will pour out my spirit on you and tell you what I think.
1:24: I called, but you would not listen. I reached out my hand, but nobody paid attention.
1:25: You ignored all my advice and would not take my correction.
1:26: So when trouble comes, I will laugh; when you are afraid, I will not feel sorry for you.
1:27: Fear will come at you like a strong wind, and trouble like a storm; pain and worry will come upon you.
1:28: Then you will call me, but I will not answer; you will look everywhere for me, but you will not find me.
1:29: That is because you hated knowing things, and did not want to respect the LORD.
1:30: You would not take my advice, and you looked down on every correction I gave.
1:31: So you will eat the fruit of what you planted, and get your fill of your own plans.
1:32: Simple people are killed by turning away, and fools are destroyed by not caring.
1:33: But whoever listens to me will live safely, and rest quietly with nothing to fear.
